newsitem.title: USA: Norfolk Southern seeks expedited hearing.
newsitem.headline: Norfolk Southern seeks expedited hearing.

text.p: Norfolk Southern Corp has asked a U.S. District Court for an expedited hearing in its suit to block Conrail Inc's intended merger with CSX Corp, according to court documents.
Norfolk also asked the court, in a growing battle among rail industry leaders, to allow it expedited access to documents related to the merger.
Norfolk is also seeking to take depositions from top executives involved in the proposed merger, including Conrail Chairman David LeVan and CSX Chairman John Snow.

Norfolk Southern, which made a rival bid for Conrail on Wednesday, said a quick hearing was needed to forestall a November 14 Conrail shareholder meeting to facilitate the merger, and the November 15 expiration of an initial CSX tender offer for 19.9 percent of Conrail shares.
"Conrail's fate will be determined in just 16 business days," Norfolk Southern said in its request, filed in U.S. District Court for Eastern Pennsylvania.

"To prevent immediate and irreparable harm to itself and Conrail's shareholders, plaintiffs request that this court set a schedule for expedited proceedings, including a preliminary injunction hearing, and allow plaintiffs to take expedited discovery to prepare for that hearing."
A court official said a scheduling conference with parties in the case would be held Thursday, and a date for the hearing would be set sometime after the meeting.
Norfolk Southern said it wanted to take depositions from Snow on October 31, and LeVan on November 1.

It also asked for access to documents related to approval of the deal by Conrail's board, including what advantages Conrail directors stood to gain in the deal, what they knew about Norfolk Southern offers to buy the company, and defensive mechanisms built into the deal.

In the request, Norfolk Southern expanded on its allegations that Conrail had misled its shareholders. It said Conrail had made misleading statements regarding "the fact that the investment bankers who opined on the 'fairness' of the CSX offer could not, if asked to do so, opine in good faith that the consideration offered in the CSX deal is adequate from a financial point of view."
